jobs.title: Entry-level VC hiring channel (structural note)
jobs.note: STRUCTURAL FINDING, updated 2026-10-12 after probing 118 VC/growth firms across Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and Workable: only 14 had a genuine public job board, and between them they listed 3 entry-level investment seats. Tier-1 firms (Sequoia, Benchmark, Accel, Index, Kleiner Perkins, GV, Founders Fund, Thrive, General Catalyst, NEA, Redpoint, Spark, USV, Greylock, Lux, Craft, Emergence, CRV, Felicis, Coatue, Insight, Summit, TCV, BCV, IVP) post NO public entry-level investment roles at all — a16z's board carries only 5+ yr operations and engineering reqs, and Bessemer's associate seats all require 4+ yrs. TWO TRAPS FOUND: (1) ten ATS tokens that look like tier-1 firms belong to unrelated companies — 'sequoia' is Sequoia Consulting Group (HR/benefits), 'thrive' is an Atlanta design firm, 'menlo' and 'lightspeed' are robotics companies, 'amplify' is Amplify Education, 'forerunner' is a govtech company, 'playground' is childcare software, 'tiger', 'atlas' and 'durable' are unrelated startups. Always confirm the board's About text names the fund. (2) seed firms post PORTFOLIO-company roles on their own boards (8VC's incubations, Unusual's GovSignals role, First Round's 'Founding GTM'), so a hit on a fund's board is often not a job at the fund. WHERE ENTRY-LEVEL VC ACTUALLY IS: growth-equity analyst programs that recruit like banking (JMI, Insight, Bessemer, Volition, G2 — all already on this board), multi-family offices (ICONIQ), and warm intros. For the tier-1 funds the realistic route is a 2-year analyst stint elsewhere first, or alumni outreach.
jobs.flag_note: LinkedIn VC pass 2026-09-21: Tanay's read is correct — entry-level VC is largely NOT posted as formal job listings. Ran 6 tight VC queries with LinkedIn's entry-level filter: 33 results, only 8 at VC-sounding firms, and of those most were not true entry-level VC: Venture Search is a RECRUITER not a fund; HarbourVest and Adams Street are PE fund-of-funds associate (experienced); RA Capital is biotech crossover; Goanna is a hedge fund. Only genuine finds were Bain Capital 2027 Liquid Structured Credit (added) and Leonis Capital Associate. WHY: small funds hire 1-2 analysts a year through partner POSTS on LinkedIn/X, warm intros and newsletters — none of which appear in LinkedIn's jobs API, which is the only LinkedIn surface reachable without auth. John Gannon's VC jobs blog is the main aggregator for exactly these but renders its listings dynamically (101KB page, zero parseable job links). CONCLUSION: the 8 live VC entries on this board are close to the full set of FORMALLY POSTED 2027 VC analyst roles. Further VC coverage needs manual channels — following fund partners, John Gannon's newsletter, and the alumni outreach already running on this board.

jobs.title: Pixar hiring channel (structural note)
jobs.note: STRUCTURAL FINDING, 2026-10-15. Pixar is on your input sheet but had never produced a posting, and this explains why. Pixar does NOT hire through Disney's main Workday board — searching that board for 'Emeryville' returns zero results, and the 39 hits for 'Pixar' are all Disney corporate roles that merely mention Pixar in boilerplate. Pixar runs its own separate Workday tenant, linked from pixar.com/careers: https://pixar.wd501.myworkdayjobs.com/Pixar_External_Career_Site (tenant 'pixar', host 'wd501'). THAT BOARD CURRENTLY HOLDS FOUR POSTINGS IN TOTAL, per the API's own count: Line Cook (On-Call), On-Call Chef, Senior Research Scientist, and Staff Systems Engineer (Data Streaming). Nothing business, finance, strategy, production or entry-level. Its detail endpoint returns 406, the same block Disney's does, so descriptions cannot be read. THE ONLY REAL EARLY-CAREER DOOR AT PIXAR IS ITS INTERNSHIP AND RESIDENCY PROGRAM, not full-time hiring. The Pixar Undergraduate Program (PUP) is a Technical Director track, but Pixar's internship/residency areas have historically included Production Management and Business Operations, and eligibility has extended to people who graduated within a year of the start date — which would make a Summer or Fall 2027 residency reachable after a May 2027 graduation, though it is not a full-time 2027 start. Applications for those have historically opened in the winter (the Summer 2025 PUP deadline was 2 February 2025), so the action is to check pixar.com/careers in January, not now. Checking this board costs one API call, so it is worth including in routine sweeps despite being almost always empty.

jobs.title: TIME/Statista top-50 VC firms — per-firm audit (structural note)
jobs.note: STRUCTURAL FINDING, 2026-10-21 — checked all 50 firms in TIME/Statista's 'America's Top Venture Capital Firms of 2026' top 50 (the ranking covers 350 firms; TIME renders the table as a client-side Statista widget that cannot be read, and ranks 51-350 sit behind an email gate, so only the top 50 were obtainable, via a secondary write-up rather than TIME's own table). RESULT: 14 of the 50 appeared to have a public board, but FIVE of those were token collisions belonging to unrelated companies — 'sequoia' on Ashby is Sequoia Consulting Group (an HR/benefits firm), 'lightspeed' is a Northbrook IL robotics and construction company, 'insight' on Greenhouse is Insight Enterprises (a Fortune 500 IT integrator), 'forerunner' is the govtech product company, and 'eclipse' could not be confirmed as the VC. That leaves NINE genuine boards: a16z, Khosla, Bessemer, Battery, Kleiner Perkins, 8VC, First Round, Greycroft and Alumni Ventures, carrying 52 postings between them. Of those 52, exactly TWO are open to a 2027 undergraduate, both at Alumni Ventures (#44). Everything else is senior (a16z's entire board is 3-10+ yrs; Bessemer's only seat is 6+; Alumni Ventures' other ten are 7-10+), an MBA internship (Greycroft), a class-of-2028 internship (Battery), a design/engineering fellowship (Kleiner Perkins), or a role at a portfolio/incubated company rather than the fund (8VC, First Round). THIRTY-SIX of the top 50 have no public board at all — including Accel, General Catalyst, Founders Fund, Benchmark, Greylock, NEA, Thrive, Lux, Menlo, CRV, Redpoint, Felicis and Tiger. This is not a gap in the search; it is how the industry hires. Conclusion: ranking position is uncorrelated with accessibility, and the route into these firms is a 2-year analyst stint elsewhere or alumni outreach, not applications. See also the existing 'Venture capital | Entry-level VC hiring channel' note on this board.
